h1: Nuclear licensing consultants in 2026: who reactor developers actually hire
meta_title: Nuclear licensing consultants 2026: the complete NRC support map
meta_description: Who reactor developers hire for NRC licensing in 2026: Jensen Hughes, Enercon, Sargent & Lundy, Certrec, EXCEL, the law firms, and the AI platforms, with real cost anchors: NRC's $318 hourly rate, NuScale's $500M application, and TerraPower's 18-month review.
tldr: Advanced reactor developers assemble NRC licensing support from four pools. Consultancies: Jensen Hughes, Enercon, Sargent & Lundy, Certrec, EXCEL Services, and MPR do application preparation, environmental reports, and RAI defense. Law firms: Morgan Lewis has held Chambers Band 1 for nuclear regulatory work for more than a decade. AI platforms: Atomic Canyon (search over ADAMS), Everstar (generated a 208-page license application chapter in about a day in a DOE demonstration), Nuclearn (plant operations), and Invariant, whose Helion-512 retrieval model is the published state of the art on FermiBench and whose agents draft licensing documents with a forward-deployed engineer owning the work. The stakes are written in the costs: NRC review time bills at $318 per hour ($148 for advanced reactors), and NuScale's design certification application took over $500 million and 2 million labor hours.

sections.heading: The four pools of NRC licensing support
paragraphs: No reactor developer licenses alone. Even the teams celebrated for in-house licensing bought help: Kairos Power ran its Hermes construction permit campaign with an internal regulatory affairs organization and got the first non-LWR construction permit in 50 years, and X-energy's Long Mott project still used Sargent & Lundy for site selection, licensing, and environmental support. The build-or-buy question is really a portfolio question across four pools: engineering consultancies, law firms, AI platforms, and your own staff.

What changed in 2025 and 2026 is the fourth pool. AI systems moved from demos to the licensing workflow itself: a DOE Genesis Mission demonstration had Everstar's Gordian generate a 208-page chapter of an NRC license application in about a day, work DOE described as typically taking an expert team 4 to 6 weeks. Invariant runs the same class of work as a service: agents draft licensing documents with every claim traced to its source, and a forward-deployed licensing engineer owns the output. The consultancies and firms are not going away; the drafting economics underneath them are moving.

sections.heading: The consultancies: who does what
paragraphs: The incumbent bench is deep and specialized. Jensen Hughes runs a dedicated nuclear licensing and regulatory support practice, with over 300 nuclear and power engineers drawn from the NRC, NEI, EPRI, and utilities, and particular strength in fire protection, seismic, and PRA work that feeds licensing. Enercon is the environmental report powerhouse: it prepared the environmental report and limited work authorization for Holtec's Palisades SMR-300 construction permit application, accepted by the NRC in February 2026, and the environmental assessment behind the Palisades restart. Sargent & Lundy describes itself as involved in nearly all ongoing SMR and advanced reactor projects, designed NuScale's VOYGR nuclear island, and carried the siting, licensing, and environmental work behind the Dow and X-energy Seadrift application.

Certrec is the closest thing to an incumbent software-plus-services hybrid: it has produced more than 100 major licensing submittals for NRC filing and managed the electronic production of NuScale's standard design approval application through its Taktix workflow platform. EXCEL Services, founded in 1985, is the license renewal and license amendment specialist, and, tellingly, an investor in Everstar. MPR Associates advises advanced reactor developers across molten salt, sodium fast, high temperature gas, and microreactor designs. None of them publishes rates; the anchor that exists is the NRC's own billing: $318 per hour full-cost in FY2025, cut to $148 per hour for advanced reactor applicants.

sections.heading: The law firms
paragraphs: Nuclear regulatory law is unusually concentrated. Morgan Lewis is the only firm Chambers USA has ranked Band 1 for nuclear regulatory and litigation work for more than a decade, and it hired the NRC's former general counsel in 2025. Pillsbury carries the heritage of the original nuclear buildout and stays active in novel licensing strategies, including fusion and accelerator-driven systems. Hogan Lovells is strong on export control and fuel cycle work, and Balch & Bingham holds the Southern Company and Vogtle lineage. Use them for what only counsel does: hearings, enforcement, contested proceedings, novel legal interpretations, and privilege. The bulk of a licensing campaign, drafting safety analysis chapters, environmental reports, and RAI responses, is engineering documentation, not legal argument.

sections.heading: What NRC licensing actually costs
paragraphs: The published numbers deserve to be stated plainly, because they explain the entire services market. The National Academies put the applicant-side cost of assembling the tests, analyses, and documentation for a license application at up to many hundreds of millions of dollars, with NRC fees adding many tens of millions. NuScale's design certification application consumed over $500 million and more than 2 million labor hours, backed by over 2 million pages of supporting information. On the agency side, a typical early site permit runs around 29,000 NRC review hours, about $9 million in fees at the full-cost rate.

The direction of travel is compression. TerraPower's Natrium construction permit went from submission in March 2024 to a permit in March 2026, with the technical review finished in under 18 months against a 27-month schedule. Kairos prepared its Hermes application in 18 months from the decision to build. Executive Order 14300 now imposes an 18-month decision deadline on the NRC. Faster reviews concentrate the remaining schedule risk exactly where developers control it: how quickly and consistently the applicant side can produce and defend documents.

sections.heading: The AI layer, honestly mapped
paragraphs: Four companies define AI for nuclear licensing in 2026, and they are not interchangeable. Atomic Canyon builds Neutron, AI search over the NRC's roughly 53 million page ADAMS corpus, with deployments at Diablo Canyon, partnerships with Oak Ridge and Idaho National Laboratory, and a cooperation agreement with the IAEA signed in December 2025: excellent retrieval, not application drafting. Everstar's Gordian is a generation platform, and its DOE Genesis Mission demonstration, a 208-page license application chapter produced in about a day, is the clearest public evidence yet that drafting automates. Nuclearn, with a $10.5 million Series A and deployments at over 70 facilities, is a plant operations platform: corrective actions, engineering evaluations, equipment diagnostics, not licensing.

Invariant's position in that map: Helion-512, its nuclear-domain retrieval model, is the published state of the art on FermiBench, the public retrieval benchmark for the nuclear regulatory domain, and the platform pairs that retrieval with agents that draft licensing documents, every claim traced to its source, plus a forward-deployed licensing engineer who owns the work end to end. The full head-to-head, including Inductive and evaluation criteria, is in our AI for NRC licensing comparison. The short version of the difference: search tools find the precedent, generation tools produce a draft, and Invariant ships the document with a named engineer accountable for it.

sections.heading: How to assemble your licensing bench
paragraphs: A pattern that holds across the recent successful campaigns: a small in-house regulatory core that owns strategy and the NRC relationship, specialist consultants for the showings that need deep bench strength, siting, environmental, PRA, seismic, counsel reserved for contested and privilege-sensitive matters, and, increasingly, an AI layer carrying the drafting volume. The applicant-side documentation grind is the largest controllable cost in the table above, and it is the part Invariant removes: agents produce the drafts and trace every requirement, the forward-deployed engineer owns quality and delivery, and the incumbents on this page remain what they are, the right tools for the work that genuinely needs them.

faqs.question: Who are the main nuclear licensing consultants?
faqs.answer: The names that recur across current NRC licensing campaigns: Jensen Hughes (licensing and regulatory support, fire protection, PRA), Enercon (environmental reports, including Holtec's Palisades SMR-300 application), Sargent & Lundy (siting, licensing, and environmental work across most active SMR projects), Certrec (licensing submittal production, over 100 major NRC filings), EXCEL Services (license renewals and amendments), and MPR Associates (advanced reactor regulatory advice). Morgan Lewis leads among law firms, and an AI layer (Atomic Canyon, Everstar, Nuclearn, Invariant) now carries growing parts of the work.

NuScale's design certification took over $500 million and 2 million labor hours. NRC review time bills at $318 per hour in FY2025, reduced to $148 per hour for advanced reactor applicants, and a typical early site permit consumes about 29,000 review hours, roughly $9 million in fees.

faqs.question: How long does an NRC construction permit take now?
faqs.answer: Faster than the historical reputation suggests. TerraPower's Natrium construction permit went from March 2024 submission to a March 2026 permit, with the technical review completed in under 18 months. Kairos Power's Hermes and Hermes 2 permits cleared on accelerated reviews, and Executive Order 14300 now sets an 18-month decision deadline for the NRC. The binding constraint is increasingly the applicant's own document production, not the regulator's queue.

faqs.question: Do I need a law firm or a consultant for NRC licensing?
faqs.answer: Different jobs. Law firms (Morgan Lewis has held Chambers Band 1 for nuclear regulatory work for over a decade) handle hearings, enforcement, contested proceedings, and privilege-sensitive questions. Consultancies handle the engineering showings: safety analysis, siting, environmental reports, PRA. Most of a licensing campaign is engineering documentation, which does not legally require counsel, and its drafting is what AI platforms like Invariant now automate with an accountable engineer in the loop.

In a DOE Genesis Mission demonstration, Everstar's Gordian generated a 208-page chapter of an NRC license application in about a day, work DOE said typically takes an expert team 4 to 6 weeks. Regulator-facing responsibility stays with humans; the drafting volume no longer has to.
